role: paper-level multiplicity boundary for the two predeclared secondary site-template-resistant TNC diagnostics
standalone_reporting: Each member retains its frozen two-sided 95% interval and standalone secondary classification.

family_claim_rule.method: Bonferroni for two predeclared secondary tests
family_claim_rule.allowed_claim: A paper-level statement that site-template-resistant TNC evidence is supported requires at least one member's 97.5% family interval entirely in its prespecified positive direction.
family_claim_rule.opposite_direction: A member whose 97.5% family interval is entirely below 0 is family-level contradicted-direction evidence for that member.
family_claim_rule.neither: If neither 97.5% family interval excludes 0 in the positive direction, do not claim family-level support even if one standalone 95% interval is positive.

no_rescue: Do not add a third site-template-resistant diagnostic after future outcomes are opened and retain a two-test correction.
Do not select whichever diagnostic has the narrower interval and omit the other.
Neither secondary diagnostic can rescue a null authoritative four-bay static TNC primary.
Family-level support weakens a purely time-invariant site-template explanation but does not eliminate time-varying common causes, persistent meter-mark microhabitat or TNC measurement error.
